descriptionHtml:
Decision D6 · P1 · Daniela

Transcript / retention windows differ from UAT 3.6 in ways no ticket AC settles: archive 48 h (not 36), 'Earlier sessions' and 'Most Recent' are undated, Quick Dictation boxes never expire, windows are hard-coded (make them configurable?); the Nursing Home course card shows the last 3 visits (UAT 3.6 says 2) (Q5)

Other cases of the same question (counted once): TC-16/S23, TC-16/S27, OAT-04/S19, TC-11/S28, TC-11/S07

Approach · TC-04 Quick Dictation (Hospital only; TC-05 Rounding Sheet merged in) · S10 How long an unassigned and an assigned box stay on the pad (12 / 18 / 36 h ± 1 h)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U4 An unassigned box stays on the pad after Quick Dictation is closed and reopened, as the physician's own log. Boxes are never silently dropped. (The UAT says 'stays on the sheet'; … (UAT TC-04; TFA-92582 AC 5; TFA-92582 step 5; TFA-92583 AC 4)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given One unassigned and one assigned box created at T

When Age the boxes to T+11 h, T+13 h, T+17 h, T+19 h, T+35 h, T+37 h on the server clock, and set the device clock wrong by a day

Then Boxes stay or clear exactly at the window Q6 settles on, never silently before it, and the same on every device clock

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): U4 (never silently dropped) against the window Daniela gives for Q6; 3.6 has no row for boxes, so the expected window is unknown today. 3.8: server clock, not device clock

Where it ran: local code-review (judged by reading the code); test method CODEREVIEW · Code review; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S10 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-04.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row; to be decided by Daniela; the Allure status was changed by the triage from unknown to failed.

Issue type: Needs a decision (Daniela) · environment local · tickets TFA-92582 ready for qa; TFA-92583 ready for qa

Quick Dictation boxes never expire, assigned or not: they stay on the pad until the physician deletes them, so nothing is lost silently, but no 12, 18 or 36 h clearing happens either.

Evidence: code-review partial. The code-decidable half passes: there is no cron or lifecycle for quickDictationDrafts, and every delete is a person's action with an audit row. Open: Q6 (Daniela) on the retention window. If she sets one, nothing in the code applies it yet. Q14: the hidden Rounding Sheet filters placed boxes by the device clock. The TIME-lane ageing run was not done.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane code-review.

Test method: CODEREVIEW · Code review (CODEREVIEW (quickDictationDrafts has only _creationTime and assignedAt; no cron or lifecycle clears it, crons.ts holds only the session sweep)); secondary: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: code-review.

UAT item: TC-04 Quick Dictation (Hospital only; TC-05 Rounding Sheet merged in) · Section: A1 · Home Screen & Dashboard · Scenario: TC-04/S10

How long an unassigned and an assigned box stay on the pad (12 / 18 / 36 h ± 1 h)

Tickets: TFA-92582 Quick Dictation (ready for qa); TFA-92583 Rounding Sheet (ready for qa)

New local lane code-review: status partial in code-review/results.json → needs a person (partial: the half that can be checked passed, the other half needs another lane / a person / a file → a person looks).

Detail:

At e02167f, Quick Dictation boxes have no retention window at all: no 12, 18 or 36 h, no TTL and no timed clean-up. The only cron (apps/web/convex/crons.ts) is the hourly expired-session sweep, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts never mentions quickDictationDrafts. A box can be deleted in only three ways, and each one is a person's action carried out on the server:
(1) quickDictation.remove, called only from deleteCompartment when the physician taps delete in the Quick Dictation modal or on the sheet;
(2) quickDictation.clear, which the client wires up in data/rounding.ts but never calls;
(3) account deletion (account.ts), which removes boxes with via "account_deleted".
Every delete writes an audit row. Assigning a box marks it and never deletes it. The pad lists every box the user owns, sorted by order, with no time filter, so the device clock never removes or hides a box from the pad.
One device-clock rule exists, but it is outside the pad: the Rounding Sheet (hidden, Q14) shows an assigned box under its patient only if assignedAt falls on today's date by the device clock (compartmentsPlacedToday / isToday). The box itself stays on the pad.
So the code-decidable rule passes: nothing drops a box silently. Whether boxes should clear at a set window is left to Q6, which the oracle says does not decide this verdict. Today the code would keep both boxes past T+37 h on any clock.

Open questions (openQuestions):

  • Q6 window: the code has no retention window for Quick Dictation boxes. Unassigned and assigned boxes stay until the physician deletes them (or deletes the account), so they never clear at 12, 18 or 36 h. If Daniela sets a window, there is no code for it yet.
  • Q14: if 'stays on the sheet' turns out to mean the Rounding Sheet, assigned boxes there are filtered to 'placed today' by the device clock (roundingSheet.ts isToday). That would conflict with 3.8 (server clock, not device clock).
  • Q6 (Daniela): the code has no retention window for Quick Dictation boxes, assigned or unassigned. They stay until the physician deletes them (or clears the pad, or deletes the account). If Q6 sets a 12, 18 or 36 h window, nothing in the code would apply it, and the 'clear exactly at the window' half would then fail.
  • Q14: the Then is read against the pad. The hidden Rounding Sheet filters assigned boxes by a 'today' check on the device clock. If the sheet is turned on, a wrong device date would hide those boxes from it, which goes against 'the same on every device clock'.

Not decidable from the code (notDecidableByCode):

  • Q6 window (pending Q6 (Daniela))
  • ageing run (TIME (T+11..37 h on a moved server clock))
  • What retention window boxes should have (Q6, Daniela).
  • Behaviour actually seen when the server clock is moved (TIME lane ageing run).
  • The window boxes should clear at (Q6, Daniela).
  • The live ageing run on a moved server clock and a wrong device clock (TIME lane) confirms the behaviour but is run by another lane.

Review verdict (verdict): pass

Evidence: 2 attached.

Dev run: skipped: not runnable on dev — not-runnable-on-dev: outside-runner (manual: needs-aging-helper). This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
